areas.name: Beverley Hills
areas.excerpt: This area, west of Seeley to Western south of 90th-95th, is the newest section of Beverley Hills, rapidly growing. The major portion of new construction started about 2 years ago, then fell off until the spring of 1939 when extensive building was resumed.

areas.name: Beverley Hills, Ill.
areas.excerpt: It is restricted to residences and well protected by the forest preserve on the north, and the Rock Island Suburban to the east. It is interesting to note that many of these old buildings are now being modernized on a big scale. Vacant property has doubled in value since 1935.

areas.name: Chicago, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a high class apartment house section fronting on Lincoln Park with all the advantages accruing from Lake Michigan proximity. There are several vacant parcels of land along the drive which will probably be improved with equally high class buildings when construction of apartment houses gains some momentum.

areas.name: Chicago, Ill.
areas.excerpt: An attempt is now being made, however, to secure a public school location east of Dearborn St. and north of Chicago Ave., with a district restriction to confine attendance to only those children living east of Clark.

areas.name: Edgebrook
areas.excerpt: This steadily developing section of good houses is a most uniform development attracting a desirable class of home owner. Area now is about 10% built and future appears on upward trend. Competition of newer houses has affected prices on older structures, but demand continues stable. Streets were partially paved by WPA.

areas.name: Evanston, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is one of the most uniform sections in Evanston. Properties are comparatively new and vacant ground in the section is being developed with houses similar to those already here.

areas.name: Evanston, Ill.
areas.excerpt: Mortgage money is more or less restricted above $16,000, as a matter of policy by institutional lenders, and not because the area does not warrant complete financing.

areas.name: Glencoe, Ill.
areas.excerpt: It has good elevation and in the main restricted to improvements of $17,500 and up. The area was subdivided in 1928 and is now about 30 per cent built. Further building continues on a modest scale and the general character of the district is improving. Schools are convenient, but transportation is somewhat distant.

areas.name: Glencoe, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a very desirable section now about 75 per cent built, improving slightly as new construction comes into the district. The ground here is rather low in comparison to adjoining sections, but it is not considered particularly objectionable. Construction is very sound; most properties are very well held.

areas.name: Glencoe, Ill.
areas.excerpt: Lots are restricted to a minimum of 70 ' for the most part and on up to a minimum of 1/5 of an acre. The ground has good elevation, and is gently rolling and quite generally wooded.

areas.name: Glencoe, Ill.
areas.excerpt: There is a sizeable Jewish population which is supposedly better class families, and generally up to this point have not adversely affected sales to other classes. The section is inconvenient to Junior High School and somewhat distant to commuter train transportation.

areas.name: Glencoe, Ill.
areas.excerpt: The neighborhood is restricted against Jewish, except on Maple Hill Road. The ground is beautifully wooded and slightly rolling. The neighborhood has an air of privacy and exclusiveness. Entrance to those properties north of Beach Road is by a small lane built by a private easement.

areas.name: Glencoe, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is largely an area of estates, most of which have considerable ground.

areas.name: Glencoe, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a comparatively new and uniform neighborhood in East Glencoe, bordering on the Winnetka city line. The area is now about 90% improved and the few vacant lots are receiving a small amount of good construction. There have been 14 new houses built in here during the past five years.

areas.name: Highland Park, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a small, secluded area of fine homes built in a well wooded section and adjoining a country club at the south end. The ground now is about 15 per cent built and altogether there are no more than 35 houses.

areas.name: Highland Park, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This section is about 98 per cent improved, but most properties have considerable ground. There is vast room for development should any of these large estates be broken up.

areas.name: Highland Park, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This area is about 80 per cent built. The ground is quite generally flat, but it is well wooded and there are a couple of ravines which add charm to the district.

areas.name: Highland Park, Ill.

The district has fewer trees than other residential districts of Highland Park, but it is not barren in appearance. The houses on Marion Avenue are somewhat less expensive than the balance.

areas.name: Highland Park, Ill. "Deere Park"
areas.excerpt: On Lakewood Place, Lakeview Terrace, and Deere Park Drive property owners have a cooperative beach agreement which is practically equivalent to riparian rights, even though all the properties do not run to the water.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Upper class- upper middle class- executive & professional men

areas.name: Kenilworth, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is one of the most desirable residential neighborhoods along the shore. This area has uniform improvements, all beautifully kept, with fine shade trees and shrubs. Proximity to Lake Michigan is favorable. The ground is flat and about 90% built.

areas.name: Kenilworth, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This small area is comparatively new, but there are several older frame units scattered through the southern part of the district. Although they do not adversely affect values, they detract somewhat from the uniform appearance of the newer improvements.

areas.name: Kenilworth, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a uniform and high grade of good houses, conveniently located to schools, transportation, and shopping centers. The ground is slightly rolling; about 65% improved; and new construction continues at a fairly steady rate.

areas.name: Lake Forest, Ill.
areas.excerpt: These few streets are being slowly developed with good houses. Area is now about 20 per cent built and improving in desirability as new construction continues. Ground is slightly rolling, well wooded and rather secluded.

areas.name: Lincolnwood, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a high-class and well restricted residential community of outstanding individual homes. It is favorably affected by its proximity to Sauganash on the south and, in the main, takes its character from that development. The ground is about 15% improved, but all streets are paved and sidewalks are in.

areas.name: River Forest Manor in Elmwood Park, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This area is less than 10% developed with the bulk of the structures concentrated near North Ave. The neighborhood is improving as additional building take place and the adjoining vacant ground on the east may take its character from this section.

security_grade_fields.location: River Forest Manor in Elmwood Park, Ill.

areas.name: River Forest, Ill.
areas.excerpt: Ashland Ave. is restricted to dwellings costing $40,000 on 100' lots. However, this restriction is, at present, being fought by an influential property owner and probably will be defeated. Land values are about $80. a front foot. Desirability diminishes approaching North Ave., which is likely to develop commercially.

areas.name: River Forest, Ill. "North Woods"
areas.excerpt: This area is older than the adjacent first grade area to the north, and is the location of the most expensive residential construction in River Forest. Terrain is level with very fine large trees and double planting along most streets.

areas.name: Sauganash
areas.excerpt: This neighborhood is one of the best residential communities within the city limits of Chicago. The general reputation of the area is first-class and its continued development is attracting a good class of home owner.

areas.name: Wilmette, Ill.
areas.excerpt: These two streets in spite of their age warrant special consideration because of the outstanding reputation of the area as a residential neighborhood. There are still several lots on which building can occur, but this ground is so strongly held and at such high prices that it is rather slow in happening.

areas.name: Wilmette, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a very high grade area of considerable social standing and good class improvement. Properties along Lake Michigan are probably the most desirable because they retain their riparian rights, but those west of Sheridan Road are more uniform and in constant demand.

areas.name: Wilmette, Ill. "Indian Hills Estates"
areas.excerpt: That portion east of Illinois has a minimum restriction of $12,500, whereas that west of Illinois has a minimum restriction of $25,000. The entire area has a restriction of 60 foot minimum frontages and face brick or masonry all around.

areas.name: Wilmette, Ill. "Kenilworth Gardens"
areas.excerpt: This neighborhood known as "Kenilworth Gardens" has been primarily developed in the last five years, although there are a few houses as old as ten. Most lots are 50' size, and this is one of the few sections where the ground is slightly rolling.

areas.name: Winnetka, Ill.
areas.excerpt: The section is restricted to one-half acre lots, with a few properties running as large as five acres. Although it is rather distant to transportation, it continues to improve with further development, and has a good class, modern, attractive and uniform building.

areas.name: Winnetka, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is all riparian property with the exception of the houses on Fuller Lane, and the public park property. This is again primarily a section of estate type property and lots are very deep as they run from Sheridan Road to the lake. Riparian ground values for vacant frontage is $300 a foot.

areas.name: Winnetka, Ill.
areas.excerpt: The neighborhood is well restricted, has large lots, a very good reputation, and social advantages accruing to residents from the adjoining Indian Hill Country Club. The ground is now 40 per cent developed with most properties a minimum of one-half acre by two acres.

areas.name: Albany Park
areas.excerpt: This neighborhood is feeling the influence of the Jewish section adjoining on the south. Mortgage lenders are not too anxious to lend in the area because of heavy foreclosure in the neighboring area.

areas.name: Avalon Highlands
areas.excerpt: Flat with some small landscaping. Schools, churches and shops convenient. The area lies along the IC, affording exceptional transportation advantages. High land values precluded single family construction, and about 70 per cent of the buildings are 6 to 24 flat structures.

areas.name: Avalon Park
areas.excerpt: Flat and well landscaped. Building lots are principally 30' in width. Excellent transportation; schools, shops, churches and good recreational facilities convenient. This area is marked by a very high percentage of home ownership, and houses show pride of possession.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: "White collar"- professional- mechanics- mill foremen- railroad men

areas.name: Bellwood, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is the southeastern corner of the village of Bellwood, built up almost solidly with single brick, 5-6 room bungalows. The development is about 12 years old and still of uniform and good appearance. The terrain is flat with few trees.

areas.name: Bellwood, Ill. "Miami Park"
areas.excerpt: This area is somewhat isolated and entirely surrounded by unimproved tracts of land. The area is zoned for brick single dwellings and building lots are worth about $1,200, altho there are special assessments against many of the lots remaining unpaid in amounts as high as $2,000. This was for paving and utilities.

areas.name: Berwyn
areas.excerpt: The terrain is level. Homes are well kept and uniform in type with mat lawns and trees along the sidewalk. There is a very good local retail shopping and amusement center along Cermak Road.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Skilled mechanics- office workers- small manufacturers

areas.name: Berwyn
areas.excerpt: This is a shade less desirable than the adjacent "B" ara on the west. Properties are a little older and not quite so well kept. Landscaping and trees are not quite so good. Institutions lend readily but on slightly more conservative terms than in the area above mentioned.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: White collar class- small business men- craftsmen

areas.name: Beverley Hills. Located So. Of 103-107 W. of Campbell to Country Club

areas.name: Beverly Hills

areas.name: Broadview, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This small area is bounded by the village line of Maywood on the north and by underdeveloped territory west and south. To the east lies the poorer section of the village of Broadview. The terrain is flat with few small trees.

areas.name: Broadview, Ill.
areas.excerpt: A new development lying south of the railroad and adjacent on the east is a large, U.S. Veteran Hospital. This area is bordered on the west and south by totally unbuilt tracts and on the north by the village of Maywood. Streets are unpaved and all sidewalks are not yet in.

areas.name: Brookfield, Ill. "Hollywood"
areas.excerpt: Flat and partially wooded with elm, oak and maple trees. Bounded on the north by the Chicago Zoological Park (Brookfield Zoo) and a suburban electric railway. Schools are very convenient, transportation is good. The area is about 60 per cent built up.

Location is very desirable but newer building at other points along Lake Shore Drive have attracted the better class families. One-family houses are concentrated east of Sheridan Road and north of Diversey parkway.

areas.name: Chicago

areas.name: Chicago
areas.excerpt: This section is known as Streeterville. Practically all buildings are either apartments or apartment hotels.

areas.name: Chicago, Ill.
areas.excerpt: The Polish influence noted above is of only moderate proportion, and it is generally considered to be a better class family and not adversely affecting the desirability of the are. Because of uniformity of improvements and general desirability, the territory is graded "B-".

areas.name: Chicago, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a substantial area of good housing, now about 90 per cent built up. Area is very clean and pride of ownership apparent throughout. Transportation is convenient, but slow to downtown Chicago, as only street car services this section.

areas.name: Chicago, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a desirable residential neighborhood of brick bungalows and two family structures. Properties are in relatively good condition and the general appearance of the neighborhood is such as to continue to attract a good middle class population.

areas.name: Deerfield, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This subdivision has only about 20 houses in it at present. Ground is slightly rolling and partially wooded at the north end. Distance to Chicago Loop is objectionable to class of occupant, and closer-in areas are most competitive.

areas.name: Edison Park
areas.excerpt: This is a very desirable neighborhood of good houses well located, convenient to shopping and amusement centers. Transportation by train to downtown Chicago is very good and the general reputation of the area is above average.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Junior executives, upper middle class & middle class- $2,500-3,500

areas.name: Evanston, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a desirable residential neighborhood in northwest Evanston rather distant from shopping centers and schools and transportation facilities. Local bus transportation is available on Grant and Central St., making connections with North Shore and elevated trains at points east along Central.

areas.name: Evanston, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a rather mixed territory with the new construction centered south of Simpson. More favorably located, these new houses could be grade as first class, but their proximity to Niles Center and its taverns along Emerson St. adversely affects them.

areas.name: Evanston, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a neighborhood of predominantly six and seven room one family structures with a concentration of two family units on Eastwood north of Central. There are a few rowhouses on Broadway, which in themselves are good buildings, but this class of construction is in poor demand.

areas.name: Evanston, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This small section in north Evanston continues as a very desirable residential section of modest homes. Transportation and schools are very convenient, but shopping centers are rather distant.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Upper middle class and middle class

areas.name: Evanston, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This area known as the Orrington District is one of the most desirable in Evanston, but because the properties are of substantial age the neighborhood has been rated second class. Proximity to Northwestern University on the east is very favorable, and convenience to Lake Michigan beaches also helps the neighborhood.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Upper class and upper middle class- executive & professional men

areas.name: Evanston, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a desirable neighborhood in the south end of Evanston, which should hold up fairly well during the next five to ten years. Properties west of Ridge are primarily brick bungalows and one and one-half story houses of modest character.

areas.name: Evanston, Ill.
areas.excerpt: Each year a separate bathing beach is designated for the large colored population living in Evanston, the thought being a constant shifting of this location would minimize the adverse effect of negro bathing facilities.

areas.name: Evanston, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This neighborhood is very well located and is particularly convenient to both elevated and commuter train transportation, the latter stopping at Main St. there are about six houses on Dempster, between Judson and Forest Aves., which are and have been for a number of years, occupied by negroes.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Middle class and upper middle class

areas.name: Evergreen Park, Ill. Loc. So. Of W. 91-99th bet. Crawford & California
areas.excerpt: The population of Evergreen Park, is est. of 3200 (1940), and is situated 15 miles south of the loop. The larger part of the town has been built during the past five years. This is a suburban residential community. They have their own water system, but no sewers. They also have gas and electricity. Taxes are fair.

areas.name: Glencoe, Ill.

areas.name: Glencoe, Ill.
areas.excerpt: Properties along Euclid are somewhat larger than in the balance of the territory, but there are several Jewish families on that street which detract somewhat from its desirability.

areas.name: Glenview, Ill.
areas.excerpt: A small section about 10 per cent developed, with good houses. Area is convenient to transportation on North Shore.Electric, but distant to schools and shopping center. Trend of desirability is slowly improving. Ground is flat, but well wooded.

areas.name: Glenview, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This section is only about 10 per cent built up but development continues at a fairly good pace and trend of desirability is improving. Houses are of individual architecture and good appearance. Schools, shopping centers and transportation are distant and somewhat objectionable, but not seriously retarding development.

areas.name: Glenview, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This district is about 50 per cent built up and improving in desirability as development continues at a fairly steady pace. Houses are uniform and of good architectural appearance, but ground has few trees and district is somewhat barren.

areas.name: Golf, Ill.
areas.excerpt: A small residential community about 60 per cent built up with most improvements average 12-15 years of age. Village has commuter train stop but no shopping center or school. Section is well laid out; has only local traffic and continues as a desirable residential area.

areas.name: Highland Park, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a very sparsely settled district in the north end of Highland Park, and an attractive and well wooded district.

areas.name: Highland Park, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is the old central part of Highland Park, and although many properties might be considered obsolete a number have been reconditioned and the area continues as a desirable residential section. The ground is practically all improved, slightly rolling, and beautifully wooded.

areas.name: Highland Park, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This small section is now about 15 per cent built, and is improving slightly as additional buildings come into the section. The general appearance of the structures is good, but there are few trees in the territory and the neighborhood has a rather barren appearance.

areas.name: Highland Park, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This section is about 80 per cent built up. The ground is slightly rolling, beautifully wooded, but is somewhat adversely affected by its proximity to the railroad.

areas.name: Highland Park, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a desirable neighborhood now about 75 per cent built. The ground is slightly rolling and generally well wooded. The area is convenient to the local shopping center and the south end is rather distant to schools. There is a train stop on Roger Williams Ave. in the center of the area.

areas.name: Highland Park, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This section is about 15 per cent built with good houses in an attractive wooded area with an appealing layout and a good suburban atmosphere. Schools and transportation are convenient but shopping centers are very distant.

areas.name: Kenilworth, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This neighborhood compares favorably with the first class section directly adjoining on the east, but properties are somewhat older. This neighborhood houses a very high grade population, many of whom are wealthy, and shows evidence of pride of ownership, as properties are continually being remodeled and reconditioned.

areas.name: Kenilworth, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This neighborhood is 100 per cent improved, except for a few larger places around some of the older estate type properties. The neighborhood is well located, convenient to schools, transportation, shopping centers, and although properties are of substantial age, the neighborhood continues as a desirable one.

areas.name: Lake Bluff, Ill.
areas.excerpt: A small section of good houses now less than 10 per cent built up. The ground is slightly rolling and the eastern half is well wooded and has better properties. Trend of desirability is slightly upward, but development is slow and it is doubtful that any volume of construction will occur soon.

areas.name: Lake Forest, Ill.
areas.excerpt: The area is well laid out and improvements are attractive, but the proximity of negro families on Spruce St. at the southern edge precludes the district from a better rating, and is retarding its development.

areas.name: Lake Forest, Ill.
areas.excerpt: A desirable residential district of somewhat older structures housing good class occupants. The ground is 100 per cent improved and has fine, large, trees and attractively laid out streets. Pride of ownership is apparent, and in spite of the age of many properties, the section has great appeal and charm.

areas.name: Lake Forest, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This small section continues as a desirable area of substantial homes. Properties south of Vine Avenue run from Green Bay Road thru to the railroad tracks, but others are on 50-100 foot lots of normal depth.

areas.name: Lincolnwood, Ill.
areas.excerpt: These few blocks have recently begun to be developed with moderately priced bungalows and 2-story residences. The ground surrounding is practically all vacant, but it was subdivided prior to 1929 and most improvements are already in the ground.

areas.name: Lincolnwood, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This small tract of ground was recently opened by a local builder and development has gone ahead fairly rapidly. Most properties are of unique design and of individual architecture. The proximity to commuter train transportation on Pratt Blvd has been a favorable influence in the sale of these properties.

areas.name: Maywood, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is the only part of Maywood zone to restrict Hebrew encroachment. It is known as a "Seminary District". The area is separated by a principal boulevard, Harrison St., from an otherwise adjacent poor area at the south which lies in a neighboring village of Broadview.

areas.name: Niles Center, Ill.
areas.excerpt: A sparsely built area of multiple units in good condition, but rather inconveniently located to shopping centers and somewhat distant to Chicago loop transportation. areas.name: Niles Center, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This small section has had a recent development with good class one-family residences, and its further development may be anticipated. Proximity to Evanston Golf Club on the west is favorable. Transportation and shopping centers are inconvenient.

areas.name: Niles Center, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This neighborhood is about 10 per cent built, with the bulk of structures centered around Oakton Park. All streets are paved and it appears that future development will be similar in character to that which is already here.

areas.name: Niles Center, Ill.
areas.excerpt: These few blocks are about 90 per cent built up with modest houses and bungalows. The ground is flat and somewhat barren, but the neighborhood is still desirable and the western edge north of Oakton St. is improving with steady building of new houses.

areas.name: Niles Center, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a particularly choice piece of ground, as it lies in the territory that is considerably wooded. Its development is rather unique in that it is primarily three-family brick structures, which are rather widely scattered in an otherwise one-family village.

areas.name: Niles Center, Ill.
areas.excerpt: About 20 per cent built with modest houses. Section is isolated from all conveniences, but because of its newness and uniformity it is graded second class.

areas.name: Northfield, Ill.
areas.excerpt: Occupancy is restricted to 'whites' only. Altho this section is comparatively new, even at best it was never a first grade area, but is quite desirable because of its suburban location. The ground is flat and there are few, if any, trees.

areas.name: Northwest Chicago, Ill.
areas.excerpt: A Jewish infiltration is evident north of Peterson Avenue.

areas.name: Northwest Chicago, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This small neighborhood is one of the most desirable in the Northwest side district. Properties are of good appearance and of homogeneous character. Transportation and shopping facilities are rather inconvenient and school children must cross heavily traveled highways to schools.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Upper middle class and middle class

areas.name: Northwest Chicago, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is the most desirable residential neighborhood in this immediate community. The area houses a good middle class population and most of the properties are very well held. Proximity to Portgage Park is a favorable influence and transportation, shopping and amusement centers are adequate and convenient.

areas.name: Northwest Chicago, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This area at the present time is about 50 per cent built, with new construction continuing at a fairly steady pace. Buildings are predominately bungalow type of a rather stereotyped appearance. The older houses are centered in the northern and around Forest Glen school.

areas.name: Northwest Chicago, Ill.
areas.excerpt: Development has only recently started in this area. The ground lies well, but it is practically barren of trees and lies between two railroad lines. Buildings will probably follow the pattern of those in the section on the east rather than those in the area on the west.

areas.name: Northwest Chicago, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This territory is largely vacant at the present time, but its future appears secure and may be expected to improve with any volume of building. Those few properties now located in the section are only fair, but the territory is so favorably located that it is doubtful that they can adversely affect development.

areas.name: Northwest Chicago, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a secluded area in wooded territory fronting on the Edgebrook Golf Course. Although properties are of substantial age, the section continues as a desirable residential neighborhood, well protected against unfavorable influences.

areas.name: Norwood Park
areas.excerpt: This is a desirable neighborhood with the streets bound by Eaven, Neola and the Northwest Highway being particularly outstanding and comparing more favorably perhaps with Edison Park. The general appearance of the section is good, however, although it is somewhat mixed construction.

areas.name: Oak Park, Ill.
areas.excerpt: One negro family resides in the area, but there is no possibility whatever of any further infiltration.

areas.name: Oak Park, Ill.
areas.excerpt: At the extreme eastern edge of this area there are a few Italian families living along Humphrey and Taylor Streets at the extreme north end. There is also some tendency towards infiltration of Czechs, Polish, and Hebrews in the same neighborhood.

security_grade_fields.infiltration_of: Czechs, Polish, Hebrew- slowly into east end

areas.name: Oak Park, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a somewhat old but still desirable area bordered on the east and west by cheaper neighborhoods, and on the north by the best section of the village. Construction is mixed, old and new, large and small.

areas.name: Park Ridge, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This area compares in many ways with the section directly north, but the average age of the properties is somewhat greater and the district is not quite as uniform.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Middle class- some upper middle class

areas.name: Park Ridge, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is generally considered to be the most desirable residential neighborhood in Park Ridge. The area abuts the Chicago city limits on its eastern boundary, and is somewhat distant from the local shopping center and transportation facilities. The ground is quite flat and has only fair sized trees lining each street.

areas.name: Park Ridge, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a desirable residential district with fairly uniform houses, now about 80 per cent built, with considerable activity in new building largely centered west of Crescent Ave. near Cumberland and Gillick. Most properties are built on 50' lots and the bulk of the units give indication of pride of ownership.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Middle class- some upper middle class

areas.name: Park Ridge, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a desirable section now being steadily developed with good class houses fairly uniform in design and of good construction. The western half of the district is well wooded, the balance being somewhat barren.

areas.name: Park Ridge, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a comparatively new and desirable residential district in the southern part of Park Ridge. The ground is now about 70 per cent built and rather barren in appearance.

areas.name: Ravenswood Manor
areas.excerpt: Jewish infiltration has started along the edges and may be expected to continue because of favorable reputation and location. Houses are substantial and well appearing, but the price trend is slightly weak. Rentals are very firm, however, and occupancy virtually 100 percent.

areas.name: River Forest
areas.excerpt: This area extends between Chicago Ave. and Lake St. all the way across town. Harlem Ave., the western boundary is heavily traveled. Soo Line Railroad outs the area from north to south in the western portion.

areas.name: River Forest, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This area is divided into eastern and western sections by a first grade area of more expensive homes. Terrain is flat with excellent planting of fine trees, double rows on some streets. Bounded at north by Division St. and on the south by Chicago Ave., the latter being a boulevard with moderately heavy traffic.

areas.name: Riverdale, Ill.
areas.excerpt: The two blocks on the east Michigan to Indiana are opposite the poorer section of Dolton which is partly undeveloped with foreign infiltration and no demand for property at all. About 10 to 15 per cent of the Ivanhoe area is built up and has paved streets and sidewalks. This is a growing community.

areas.name: Riverdale, Ill.
areas.excerpt: Homes and shrubbery, are well kept, and there are no Negroes or other undesirable elements in the neighborhood. City Pop. 3,400 (est. 1940)

areas.name: Riverside, Ill.
areas.excerpt: The area is a flat, wooded peninsula with a narrow strip of forest preserve encircling it. Beyond the forest preserve is the Des Plaines River. Land values are very high here and most of the very expensive homes of Riverside are located in this tract.

areas.name: Riverside, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This section is flat and wooded, with fine, large oak and elm trees, and is adjacent to the shopping center of Riverside at the south. Many large, fine, old houses occur throughout, generally on large lots with shrubbery and landscaping.

areas.name: Riverside, Ill.
areas.excerpt: North of 31st Street is not quite so desirable because not so protected from future encroachment. The rental properties in this territory are the better homes, whereas in the second-grade area south of the railroad, the finer homes are owner-occupied.

areas.name: Riverside, Ill.
areas.excerpt: However, the influx of a Bohemian population has been considered in grading this area "B". This population, while of good quality, tends to concentrate and some houses show the European influence, which would probably render them less salable to outsiders.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Small business owners- small executives; No foreign born 50% Czech extraction
security_grade_fields.infiltration_of: This class coming in rapidly from Cicero & Berwyn

areas.name: Riverside, Ill.
areas.excerpt: Bohemian influence in the area adjacent to the east is likely to affect this section.

areas.name: Rogers Park
areas.excerpt: Although there is no concentration of Jewish in the area at the present time, it appears infiltration may be expected for they are threatening at the present time. About 10 per cent of the structures are brick two-family units valued at $9,000 to $11,000 renting for $57.50 to $65.00 per month.

areas.name: Rogers Park
areas.excerpt: This area at present is about 15 per cent built with new construction continuing at a fairly steady pace. The bulk of the new houses are five and six-room bungalows and one and one-half story residences, selling below $10,000.

areas.name: Rogers Park
areas.excerpt: This is a neighborhood of good homes with a few two and three family buildings of similar character. Indian Boundary Park is a favorable influence although it is partially surrounded on the east and north with large apartment buildings.

areas.name: Rogers Park
areas.excerpt: This small neighborhood is favorably affected by a Catholic Church on Glenwood and Loyola. The properties are well maintained and the general appearance of the section is good.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Upper middle class and middle class

areas.name: Rogers Park
areas.excerpt: There is a Jewish infiltration noticeable but they are better class families and not adversely affecting occupancy or rentals.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Middle and upper middle class- business man

areas.name: Rogers Park
areas.excerpt: There is a slight but steady infiltration of better class Jewish tenants into the section. About 10 per cent of the ground is vacant and when apartment building again revives this area should be a likely spot for such development.

areas.name: Rogers Park
areas.excerpt: This high class neighborhood is almost solidly built of good class apartments. Its proximity to the Edgewater Golf Club is a favorable influence, and the section should hold up well during the next five years.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Upper middle class and middle class

areas.name: Rogers Park
areas.excerpt: Although there are a few Jewish families in this neighborhood, no marked infiltration is noticeable at the present time, and the section should remain fairly stable during the next three to five years.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Middle class- some upper middle class

areas.name: Rogers Park
areas.excerpt: This are is similar in many respects to the section directly north of Devon, but a marked infiltration of Jewish has adversely affected values since 19937. There is a slight weakness in the price structure at the present site, although rents remain firm.

areas.name: Roseland. Loc. So of 98-107 between Indiana & Dauphin
areas.excerpt: New development today is taking place between 99th and 107th; also between Indiana Ave. and IC railroad; and is restricted to brick buildings, as today are all areas in this section. Cottage Grove, a business street, runs north and south to the east of the IC, east of area. Some new brick singles on N. Forest St.

security_grade_fields.location: Roseland. Loc. So of 98-107 between Indiana & Dauphin

areas.name: Roseland. Loc. So. Of 104-111, Emerald-Stewart
areas.excerpt: About a quarter of a mile west, at 111th street, is a large colored section.

areas.name: Roseland. Loc. So. Of 111th-1115 Stewart- Emerald
areas.excerpt: This area is about on par with the "B" area to the northeast, as a desirable place to live. The Fenger High School is in the center. It is known as one of the best high schools in Chicago. The area has all utilities, pavements, assessments in and paid for and transportation is fair.

security_grade_fields.location: Roseland. Loc. So. Of 111th-1115 Stewart- Emerald

areas.name: South Chicago
areas.excerpt: The buffer of the IC Main Line prevents any undesirable infiltration. Adjacent to the south is Jackson Park and the Rosenwald Museum. South on Cornell from 53rd, brick and stone 3-flats predominate. Some of the larger hotels and apts in the area are the Broadview, Windermere, Barclay, Chicago Beach, and Narragansett.

areas.name: South Chicago
areas.excerpt: There are a few colored people south and west around 70th and Kenwood.

areas.name: South Chicago
areas.excerpt: The majority are of brick; construction restrictions are $15,000. 71st Street is one of the better, and cleanest, business districts south of the Loop.

areas.name: South Chicago
areas.excerpt: Located between E. 67th and E. 71st, Jeffrey to South Shore Drive, predominately an apartment district, composed of 6's and up. These apartments are of the better class; the area is most desirable for those who wish to live in apartments. Transportation is good.

areas.name: South Chicago
areas.excerpt: Predominately a 2-flat area, restricted (located between 79th and 83rd, Racine to Green) as to intermingling of bungalows with flats. Lots ordinarily sell at higher prices than in the adjacent area to the west, and there are a substantial number of high-priced bungalows.

areas.name: South Chicago
areas.excerpt: A detrimental feature of this area is lack of uniform building restrictions, as bungalows, flats and large apartments are intermingled throughout. Alleys are paved. There is considerable modernization of the older buildings under way.

areas.name: South Chicago
areas.excerpt: A small area, approximately one year of age; located west of Western, between 82nd and 83rd. This recent development, financed by FHA insurance, is surrounded by vacant land.

areas.name: Southwest Chicago
areas.excerpt: Terrain is level, and as a whole about 35 per cent built up. Some blocks in south portion entirely undeveloped. This area has seen more new one-family construction in the past year than any section within two or three miles of this locality. It is the only district on the south side with 16-170 ft. deep lots.

areas.name: Washington Heights
areas.excerpt: NOTE: West of Vicennes, well over 80 per cent of properties are restricted to Whites. Loc. bet. 90th-94th, Ashland- Carpenter.

areas.name: Washington Heights
areas.excerpt: This area, lying west of Ashland- Longwood- and between 91st and 95th Streets, is the best section of this community known as Washington Heights. It is 100 per cent a bungalow area, uniform in character, presenting a good appearance. There are few homes for rent, and the average age is 10-12 years.

areas.name: Westwood in Elmwood Park, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a desirable bungalow neighborhood conveniently located to the local business district, as well as commuter train transportation. The bulk of the structures were built by one builder and financed by one of the large insurance companies.

areas.name: Wilmette, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a very desirable area of large homes convenient to Lake Michigan and accessible to a good business center along the railroad. Schools are also very good and transportation available by commuter train, North Shore Electric, as well as elevated which ends at Third and Linden.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Upper class and upper middle class

areas.name: Wilmette, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a fairly desirable neighborhood of somewhat mixed character, but of primarily one family houses of 6 to 8 room size. The poorest street is Wilmette Ave., which is an old country lane and as such was the first built up in the area.

areas.name: Wilmette, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a desirable old section similar in many instances to the area directly north, but segregated because most properties in this territory are of somewhat smaller rise.

areas.name: Winnetka, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is an area of large estates in the wooded Hubbard Woods Section. It is a beautiful piece of ground with winding roads and wooded properties, with a ravine and a small creek running along the center.

areas.name: Winnetka, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is an attractive and desirable residential section with a few older properties ranging in age up to 50 years. Most of the older properties are estate type and may be subdivided when they come into the market. The new construction is centered at the northeast corner of Green Bay Road and Tower Road.

areas.name: Winnetka, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a district now virtually completely built. The ground is all level and most streets have beautiful shade trees. There are a few older properties in the section, which are obsolete, but the district is holding up very well and continues as a desirable residential area in its price range.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Good middle class & upper middle class

areas.name: Winnetka, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a desirable community developed principally on 50 foot lots and now about 90 per cent improved, except at the northwest corner where the new construction is occurring. The recent building of a new school at Laurel and Chatfield Road will favorable affect the entire district.

areas.name: Winnetka, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is a stable and desirable residential community of somewhat mixed character with a few very expensive properties south of Willow on Chestnut, and on Linden, south of Mt. Pleasant St. The area is about 95 per cent built and the vacant ground sells for about $125.00 a foot.
Albany Park

This section is known as Portia Manor. This territory is flat and treeless, although parkways have been planted recently with elm saplings. Plotted lots are about 30 percent built up, but all vacant lots are burdened with special assessments amounting to $1,200 for each 50 feet of frontage.
Same as C-237 directly West

areas.name: Albany Park
areas.excerpt: Although properties in this section are of substantial appearance and command good rentals, the general trend of the neighborhood is definitely downward because of the marked infiltration of Jewish.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Middle class and lower middle class

areas.name: Austin
areas.excerpt: Age, rather poor appearance, lack of restrictions, and lack of demand appear to justify third grade.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: White collar workers- clerical- some skilled mechanics

areas.name: Bellwood, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is the easternmost portion of Bellwood lying between 25th Ave. and the village boundary. The terrain is flat with small trees; about 85% improved. Reasonably convenient to transportation, grammar schools and churches. Shopping facilities are located along St.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: American Can Co. employees- mechanics- laborers

areas.name: Bellwood, Ill. "Memorial Park"
areas.excerpt: This is a flat and somewhat older portion of the village built up along the Elevated Railway, and comprised of old, frame houses interspersed with a few brick bungalows not quite so old. The terrain is flat and practically treeless.

areas.name: Berwyn
areas.excerpt: Terrain is flat with some shade trees along sidewalks. It is bounded on the north by Roosevelt Road, a rather poor retail business street with surface car transportation, also Elevated Lines 4 or 5 blocks distant, north and south.

areas.name: Berwyn
areas.excerpt: Terrain is level with some planting of small trees along sidewalks. It is traversed by the Illinois Central Railroad near the south extremity, and in this vicinity are there blocks of vacant railroad property, a pumping station, and a small lumber yard. Schools and high school are convenient.

areas.name: Berwyn, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is the southernmost area of Berwyn, bordered by Lyons on the west and Stickney on the south. Appearance if fairly good with slight tapering downward at the east and better development along Clinton, Kenilworth, and Wisconsin Avenues in the west part.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Factory workers- wage earners- tradesmen- laborers

areas.name: Berwyn, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is the southeast corner of Berwyn, bordering Stickney on the south and a sparsely developed area of Cicero on the east. At the north is Ogden Ave., US Route #34, beyond which lies a fourth grade neighborhood. The area is flat, with few trees, and is about 60 per cent improved.

security_grade_fields.mortagage_funds: Up to 55% by B&L;s at 6% interest

areas.name: Berwyn, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This is the older part of Berwyn. The terrain is flat with some landscaping and better trees than in most sections. In the northwest corner, west of Kenilworth, between 31st St. and the CB&Q Railroad are grouped old frame houses, still occupied by the town's "elite".

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Business men- clerks- some mechanics and technical workers
security_grade_fields.mortagage_funds: 40-50% of appraisal in west portion by B&L's. 65% of appraisal in east portion

areas.name: Blue Island, Ill.
areas.excerpt: City 1940 est. pop. 17,100. The area has all utilities, a good school, and transportation. The better class of new building during recent years has been in that section of the area north of 123rd and west of Western.

areas.name: Brookfield, Ill.
areas.excerpt: Terrain is flat and practically treeless, and about 50 per cent improved. All vacant lots have special assessments running to $1,200 for each 50 feet of frontage. This factor has operate to the detriment of rapid development in the village.

security_grade_fields.infiltration_of: Gradual infiltration Czechs from Berwyn & Cicero

areas.name: Brookfield, Ill.
areas.excerpt: Some houses here show Bohemian influence architecturally; that is, lead glass windows, ornamental fronts, which are characteristics of (the Ciceronian bungalow). High assessments prevail here on lots and, for that reason, development has been somewhat slow.

security_grade_fields.infiltration_of: Slow infiltration of good class Bohemians from Cicero and Berwyn

areas.name: Brookfield, Ill.
areas.excerpt: This section is flat, with some trees planted along parkways and sidewalks. It is the oldest portion of Brookfield and is adjacent to the principal shopping center of the village and very convenient to the railway station. Churches are located in the area and schools are conveniently near.

areas.name: Brookfield, Ill.
areas.excerpt: The area lies adjacent to the negro section of La Grange at the west. At the southern extremity is some small business along 47th Street, and just south of 47th Street is a large quarry pit. Schools, churches, and transportation are not convenient to this section and poor development is apparent throughout.

areas.name: Brookfield, Ill. "Congress Park"
areas.excerpt: There is a grammar school in the area which has some colored attendance from La Grange. To the west of this area is the colored section of La Grange. However, there has been no encroachment and none is expected.

areas.name: Brookfield, Ill. "Old Hollywood" section
areas.excerpt: This is known as the old Hollywood section. Terrain is flat and wooded with oak, elm and maple trees and is somewhat older than the adjacent blue area to the west; and contains a mixture of bungalows and two-story residences. It is bounded by the forest preserve at the east and undeveloped land at the south.

areas.name: Brookfield, Ill. "South Brookfield"
areas.excerpt: This is known as South Brookfield. This section is flat, with some trees along parkways, and is bounded on the north by the business area and by the main line of the CB&Q railroad.

areas.name: Calumet City
areas.excerpt: To the north the area adjoining an undesirable neighborhood and the second oldest part of the city, with many saloons along State Street, and on the south adjoins the oldest area, and in time the elements in the north and on the south of this area will submerge it. Est. 1940 city pop. 12,800.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Business and professional wage earners, mechanics, etc.

areas.name: Calumet City
areas.excerpt: This is a more modern area with up-to-date homes, substantially of a better grade than the "C" area to the north. There has been much rehabilitation of homes by the inclusion of air conditioning and gas heating. There is much vacant property, particularly west of Freeland Street.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Business and professional, executive, skilled mechanics, etc.

areas.name: Calumet Gateway
areas.excerpt: Terrain is flat. In the north end of this area there are several three flats. This is the most desirable portion. There are many foreclosures throughout the area, and some 3 flats have sold as low as $9,500. Prices have stiffened in the past two years since many of the foreclosed properties have been sold off.

areas.name: Chg.
areas.excerpt: This was a 1929 development which crashed badly during the depression. Much of this area is sparsely settled, the bulk of the houses being centered near Harlem Avenue.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Lower class- some lower middle class

areas.name: Chgo- Nr. North Side
areas.excerpt: An older area of predominantly houses in state of decline due largely to obsolescence. General appearance of properties is mediocre, with most houses built close to sidewalks.

areas.name: Chgo- Nr. North Side
areas.excerpt: Future of the section is one of continuing slowly decline with the gradual infiltration of somewhat less desirable population elements. Properties are built very close to sidewalks and general appearance is one of congestion and unattractiveness, although this area is not to be considered slum territory.

areas.name: Chgo- Nr. North Side
areas.excerpt: About 25% of the structures are one-family frame units valued from $2,500-4,000, renting at $20.00-3500 per month; balance larger buildings and commercial properties.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Lower class and lower middle class

areas.name: Chgo- Nr. North Side
areas.excerpt: This is a very mixed territory of all types of housing accommodations from good apartment hotels to poor rooming houses. Predominating structures are large apartments with the trend toward conversions of smaller housing units to rooming house occupancy.

security_grade_fields.occupation_or_type: Lower middle class and middle class

areas.name: Chgo.
areas.excerpt: As a whole, about 40 per cent of the ground is vacant, with the new construction centered on Neva and Nottingham, in the first two blocks south of Belmont Ave.

areas.name: Chgo.
areas.excerpt: This neighborhood built up around the Montclare station on the Chicago Milwaukee Railroad, and is therefore older than the surrounding area. Most properties are well held and house original owners.

areas.name: Chicago
areas.excerpt: The population class is now predominantly Jewish, but there is a slow infiltration of Polish families and it is believed that this infiltration will favorably affect trend of desirability, particularly in two family structures. Transportation, except near North Ave., is inconvenient.

areas.name: Chicago
areas.excerpt: Trend of desirability is steadily downward and for the past 10 years there has been a constant infiltration of Italian from closer-in town areas. Transportation is somewhat inconvenient in the western end, but schools and shopping centers are adequate and convenient.

areas.name: Chicago
areas.excerpt: Rents in the larger apartments range from $10-15 a room, although south of Jackson in the portion that is predominantly Italian there are a number of cheaper units in large buildings. There are also a number of unheated flats which rent from $25-35.00.

areas.name: Chicago
areas.excerpt: The Polish Catholic Church is a favorable influence and has tended to hold up property values. Proximity to Humboldt Park is also favorable, particularly to those properties in the northwest corner. Rents quoted above are for heated units. There are also a number of unheated flats renting from $25-30.00 a month.

areas.name: Chicago
areas.excerpt: This is a fair residential district, completely surrounded by blighted and semi-blighted areas. The ground in this parcel was originally in an estate and was not subdivided until about 25 years ago, which accounts for the fact that buildings here are substantially younger than those in adjoining sections.

areas.name: Chicago
areas.excerpt: The area has been experiencing an Italian infiltration from south of Harrison, and this population shift is very noticeable as far north as Jackson Blvd.

areas.name: Chicago
areas.excerpt: (over) Generally speaking, it is comparatively homogeneous and continues to attract fairly good class people and it is doubtful that any infiltration of noticeably less desirable tenants will soon occur.

areas.name: Chicago (N.W.)
areas.excerpt: This area is characterized by a large number of brick three story apartment buildings, most particularly concentrated near the south of the area in the vicinity of Washington Blvd, where there is considerable Jewish population. The area declines in desirability eastward, Cicero and Lake St. being the "low spot".

areas.name: Chicago (N.W.)
